### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/package.json`, `packages/services/service-storage/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via OS_STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT_SHARED (literal, a string literal in LOCAL_ROOT_SHARED_ENV))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via OS_STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT_SHARED (literal, a string literal in LOCAL_ROOT_SHARED_ENV))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/package.json`, `packages/services/service-storage/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c385d903d29fc5bb38a0a2844837e5ad5a46129c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `251733ab2e53d362969dfe47fcab84663a057a31` — the merge of head `8c0e68dffbb07ead08092d56d054d6e2b829ff74` into base `c385d903d29fc5bb38a0a2844837e5ad5a46129c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 251733ab2e53d362969dfe47fcab84663a057a31 && git checkout 251733ab2e53d362969dfe47fcab84663a057a31
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c385d903d29fc5bb38a0a2844837e5ad5a46129c 8c0e68dffbb07ead08092d56d054d6e2b829ff74 && git checkout -B drift-repro c385d903d29fc5bb38a0a2844837e5ad5a46129c && git merge --no-ff 8c0e68dffbb07ead08092d56d054d6e2b829ff74

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c385d903d29fc5bb38a0a2844837e5ad5a46129c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c385d903d29fc5bb38a0a2844837e5ad5a46129c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8c0e68dffbb07ead08092d56d054d6e2b829ff74`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #31931 body and all 4 comments (Claim 6740625879, triage 6740634338, amendment 6740695255, dev report 6742094800); PR #31950 body and its 9-file list; the net diff `489f0cea..8c0e68df` (two commits, a97bd03f + 8c0e68df); the head's check-runs. Code outside the diff (core hook dispatch, `service-cluster` `multi-replica.ts` / `split-brain-guard.ts`, `storage-target.ts`, `ci.yml`, `clause2-line.mjs`, `check-test-source-alias.mjs`) was read only to judge the diff.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

- **New env name `OS_STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT_SHARED`: right.** This is the seat-ruled name. It is read only through `declaresSharedLocalRoot` (`multi-replica-local-root.ts`), which applies `String(v).trim().toLowerCase() === 'true'`. That is the same reading as the split-brain guard's `isTrue` for `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE`, and it matches the env-vars page convention ("`true` / `false` (case-insensitive); flag-style … `1` / `0` where noted"). The PR does not note `1` / `yes` as accepted and does not accept them, so the read is consistent with repo precedent and not lenient. It is env only, as ruled: no settings key, no constructor option and no spec entry. The `storage` namespace keys and `StorageServicePluginOptions` are untouched.
- **Narrowed boot accept set: right, and it matches the ruling.** A boot that is declared multi-replica (`declaresMultiNode`), runs the composed `cluster.driver === 'redis'`, serves the local adapter and does not set the switch, which boots on `main`, now fails at `kernel:ready`. The base-vs-head `os start` legs in the PR body measure exactly this.
- **Narrowed runtime settings accept set: right, and it matches the ruling.** Under the same condition, `applySettings` refuses a swap onto `kind: 'local'`. The check sits after `needsStorageSwap`, so an unchanged target is not affected. It runs before `buildAdapterFromValues`, `swap` and `this.target =`. The result is one `error` line, a `return`, and the current adapter and `this.target` left intact. The limits snapshot is applied above the check, so a limits-only save still lands. The service is not left half-swapped.
- **Package entry exports: none added.** `src/index.ts` is not in the diff, and the `exports` map is `"."` only. `LOCAL_ROOT_SHARED_ENV`, `declaresSharedLocalRoot`, `refusesUnsharedLocalRoot` and `MULTI_REPLICA_LOCAL_STORAGE_REFUSAL` are module exports used by the plugin and its test, and they are not public. No justification is owed.
- **New dependency edge `service-storage → service-cluster`: right.** It is approved, and `service-cache` is the precedent. `service-cluster` depends only on `core` and `spec`. `core` depends on `metadata-core`, `spec` and `types`, and none of those reaches `service-storage`, so there is no cycle. The CLI already reaches `service-cluster` transitively through `service-cache` and `runtime`, so the CLI's host-resolution rule (`serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts`, which reads the CLI's own manifest) gains no new coupling. The cluster service is read duck-typed (`composedClusterDriver` → `getService('cluster').driver`), with no `instanceof`, so a second installed copy is harmless. The lockfile hunk is the one importer entry, 3 lines.
- **No new error code.** The refusal is `throw new Error(MESSAGE)`, the same shape as the split-brain guard: a pure predicate, a message constant and a throw. No `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` row is needed.

Contract hazards checked:

- **Does it fire without the declaration, or on a non-local adapter? No.** `refusesUnsharedLocalRoot` is `kind === 'local' && declaresMultiReplicaOnRedis(env, driver) && !shared`. `StorageTarget.kind` is only `'local' | 's3'`, and `init()` always sets `this.target`, so the `?? 'local'` fallback cannot be reached; if it were, it would fail closed. The memory driver, any other driver and an absent cluster service all give `false`. The CONTROL cases pin all three.
- **Is the single-node path unchanged in behaviour? Yes.** The only new work is a side-effect-free `ctx.getService('cluster')` inside `composedClusterDriver`, which never throws, and a predicate that returns `false`. The kernel's `getService` only caches and throws on a miss, and `composedClusterDriver` catches that throw.
- **Does the boot actually fail on the throw? Yes.** `ObjectKernel.bootstrap` runs `context.trigger('kernel:ready')` through `dispatchHookPropagating`, sequentially in registration order. Since #5170 / #5282, LiteKernel propagates on the boot path too. The `catch` rolls back the started plugins and rethrows before `kernel:listening` opens a socket. The dev's real `os start` measured exit 1.
- **Does `applySettings` run before the refusal reads the adapter? Yes.** Both hooks are registered at the top level of the same `start()`, the refusal hook second. The first hook `await`s `applySettings()`, and its early `return`s (`bindToSettings === false`, settings absent) end only that hook. Dispatch is sequential, so `this.target` is the post-settings adapter, as ruled. The test harness `_flushReady` uses the same sequential order.
- **Do credentials leak into messages? No.** Both messages are a constant plus fixed text. They name variable names (`OS_STORAGE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` among them) and never values.
- **Does the new edge create a cycle? No**, as shown above.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/31931-storage-local-root-replicas.md` gives `'@objectstack/service-storage': patch`. Under `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the level follows `Metadata-protocol:` alone, `none` maps to `patch`, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` bars a major. So **patch is the correct level**. The diff publishes changes to one package only: `service-storage`'s `src` and a `dependencies` entry. The docs and `vitest.config.ts` do not publish.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` appears on the PR body and on the changeset, with the arm word first inside the parentheses. It matches the amendment: the new switch widens one surface and the refusal narrows another. The title and the changeset summary both keep `!`, and the changeset carries a **BREAKING** banner, the migration (S3 or the switch) and an ADR-0087 `not-required` disposition. That disposition's claim, "no export or type of the package root changes", holds against the diff.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` appears on both, in agreement with the claim, the amendment and the triage ("Not a metadata-protocol change"). No schema, spec key or authorable metadata is touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`packages/services/service-storage/vitest.config.ts`, outside the amended surface: ACCEPTED.** It is a 6-line test-only alias (`^@objectstack/service-cluster$` → `../service-cluster/src/index.ts`), and `check:test-source-alias` forces it: that gate makes every workspace import reachable from a package's tests resolve to source, never `dist/`, and it was red on a97bd03f without the alias. The file is not built or published, and it changes no runtime. The claim's "its tests" fairly covers a package's test configuration, so no amendment is owed. As a nit, the dev report's `deviations` array does not list it as a surface breach. The PR body names it under Verification, and this record answers it.
- **Full dogfood ran on a97bd03f and was not re-run on 8c0e68df: HOLDS.** `git diff a97bd03f 8c0e68df` is exactly that one file, +6/-0. `packages/qa/dogfood/vitest.config.ts` does not import it, and it is not in any `dist`, so the dogfood suite's inputs are byte-identical across the two heads. Under `ci.yml` (THE TWO SPEEDS), the three dogfood shards run on the `merge_group` build of this exact tree, and the required `Dogfood Regression Gate` context vetoes on red there. On the PR event the aggregate concluded `success` with zero expected shards (they show as skipped), which is by design and not a dogfood verdict.
- **First closure build with `OS_SKIP_DTS=0` and the first gate sweep on a97bd03f: answered.** Both were superseded before any reading the report uses. The full plain build was redone, and all 118 derived families were re-run on 8c0e68df and reconciled (118 / 118, 0 UNRUN).
- **Out-of-scope, carrier cloud: answered.** The multi-replica Compose example (switch on a shared named volume) and Helm's move from `ReadWriteOnce` to S3 live in the cloud deploy tree, under cloud#3814. The amendment already says so, and nothing in this repo is owed.
- **Every seat ruling is met:** the read at `kernel:ready` after `applySettings`; the `service-cluster` predicates; the split-brain shape with no new code; the env-only `OS_STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT_SHARED=true`; one row in `environment-variables.mdx` and one paragraph in `self-hosting.mdx`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with `!`; the runtime swap refused with one error and the current adapter kept; and a message that names `OS_STORAGE_ADAPTER=s3` and the S3 settings.
- **Nit, not blocking:** on the boot pass, when authored `storage` settings select a *different* local root under the declaration without the switch, `applySettings` logs "…NOT applied: the current adapter keeps serving" and the boot refusal fails the process immediately afterwards. The second line is the true outcome. The first is noise on an already-refused boot.
- **Check-runs on 8c0e68df, read at 2026-11-09T14:13Z:** 21 success, 9 skipped (opt-in, push or queue-only jobs), 34 still in progress (Build / Test Core shards, Lint, Type Check, UI, Build Docs), and 0 failure, cancelled or timed out. No check-run has concluded red. The in-progress contexts are not yet a verdict, and this record does not stand in for them: landing waits on the required set concluding green.
- No must-fix. No should-fix.
